message.content:
Here’s a quick mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|----------|------------------------|
| 1 | **Psycho** | 1960 | Alfred Hitchcock | The masterclass of suspense and the iconic shower scene. |
| 2 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Stanley Kubrick | A chilling psychological descent set in an isolated hotel. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Jordan Peele | A smart blend of horror and social commentary. |
| 4 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Ari Aster | A deeply unsettling family drama that turns into pure dread. |
| 5 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | John Krasinski | Silence is survival; the tension never lets up. |
| 6 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | James Wan | A modern supernatural thriller grounded in real‑life paranormal investigators. |
| 7 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Ari Aster | A daylight horror that flips the genre on its head. |
| 8 | **It Follows** | 2014 | David Robert Mitchell | A fresh take on the “invisible stalker” trope. |
| 9 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Jennifer Kent | A psychological horror that doubles as a mother‑daughter story. |
|10 | **The Ring** | 2002 | Gore Verbinski | A creepy, atmospheric retelling of a Japanese horror classic. |
|11 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | Drew Goddard | A meta‑commentary on horror tropes that still delivers scares. |
|12 | **Suspiria (2018)** | 2018 | Luca Guadagnino | A visually stunning reimagining of the 1977 original. |
|13 | **The Witch** | 2015 | Robert Eggers | A slow‑burn, period‑accurate horror that builds dread. |
|14 | **It (2017)** | 2017 | Andy Muschietti | A nostalgic, fun‑filled adaptation of Stephen King’s novel. |
|15 | **The Others** | 2001 | Alejandro Amenábar | A moody, atmospheric ghost story with a twist ending. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want a psychological thriller, supernatural chills, or something that plays with genre expectations. Happy watching!
